title: BTS Skips Met Gala 2026 Despite Reported Invitations — Tour Gap Before Mexico City
detail: May 4, 2026 is the date of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's annual Met Gala in New York City — and BTS's scheduled rest day between the El Paso leg (May 2–3) and the Mexico City leg (May 5–10) of the ARIRANG World Tour. Multiple entertainment outlets reported that Jungkook and V (Kim Tae-hyung) had received Met Gala invitations this year, fueling widespread fan speculation about BTS making their first-ever appearance at fashion's biggest night. However, no BTS members attended the event. A viral list circulating on X (Twitter) included Jungkook and V among invited celebrities; neither appeared on the official red carpet. The May 4 rest-day gap in the ARIRANG World Tour schedule reflects standard touring logistics for cross-border travel ahead of the Mexico City run at Estadio Azteca (May 5–10 — six sold-out nights). BTS has historically maintained a low presence at Western fashion events, preferring industry music engagements. The Met Gala's 2026 theme was 'Superfine: Tailoring Black Style.'

media.caption: BTS members skip the 2026 Met Gala despite reported invitations for Jungkook and V, resting ahead of Mexico City tour leg

title: HYBE Posts All-Time Record Q1 2026 Revenue of ₩698B — BTS ARIRANG Comeback Is Primary Driver
detail: HYBE Corporation reported Q1 2026 financial results showing revenue of ₩698.35 billion (~$469M USD), the highest quarterly revenue ever recorded by the company and a double-digit percentage increase year-over-year. The BTS ARIRANG comeback — including the release of the ARIRANG album (March 2026) and the opening leg of the ARIRANG World Tour — was identified as the primary revenue driver. Merchandise, physical album sales (3.98M copies sold on Day 1 via Hanteo), streaming royalties from 'SWIM' and 'Body to Body,' and tour-related revenue all contributed. HYBE's operating profit slipped slightly from Q1 2025 due to a one-time employee stock award program, but the revenue figure set a new record for any quarter. The strong financials come amid an ongoing legal situation for HYBE founder Bang Si-hyuk, who faces a potential refiling of an investor fraud arrest warrant by South Korean police after prosecutors rejected the initial warrant request in late April 2026.

media.caption: HYBE posts record Q1 2026 revenue of ₩698.35 billion (~$469M USD), driven by BTS's ARIRANG comeback and world tour
